references.text: Jesus' claim to be the bread that comes down from heaven to give life corresponds directly to God's word that man lives by everything that proceeds from the mouth of God, and that the bread from heaven is God's gift for life.
The Psalms' description of manna as 'bread from heaven' given to the Israelites in the wilderness is the direct historical and typological precursor to Jesus as the true manna who gives eternal life.

In the same discourse, Jesus confirms that it is the Father who gives the true bread from heaven, and that this bread gives life to the world, which expands on verse 50's claim that one should not die.
The first verse after 50 explains that the bread is Jesus' flesh, given for the life of the world, and confirms that whoever eats it will live forever, in direct contrast to dying.
